subject.title: [Feature]: Non-interactive command to use Codex OAuth for model provider

question: Should OpenClaw add a non-interactive OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex OAuth setup path, and if so should it accept a callback URL, externally supplied tokens, or a safer provider-owned handoff shape?
rationale: The missing capability is real, but the permanent contract changes how OAuth material enters OpenClaw and can expose sensitive auth data if automation picks the wrong shape.

options.title: Design Safer Provider-Owned Handoff
options.body: Add the feature only after maintainers choose a validated callback or token-import contract with PKCE/state checks, redaction, docs, and security-focused tests.

options.title: Accept Callback URL Env Contract
options.body: Implement the requested env-style redirect URL import directly, with strict validation and clear documentation of the exposure risk.

options.title: Defer To Interactive And Device-Code Flows
options.body: Keep browser, device-code, and API-key setup as the supported automation surfaces until Codex exposes a stable external auth contract.

recommendation.title: Design Safer Provider-Owned Handoff
recommendation.body: Add the feature only after maintainers choose a validated callback or token-import contract with PKCE/state checks, redaction, docs, and security-focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant setup and provider-auth boundary history points most strongly to this account for the product/security shape decision.
